Test your knowledge of the material on [two-way tables](../lectures/03-Twoway1.pdf) in the following quiz to see how much you learned.
This is **entirely private for you**---no records are kept of your performance. When you've answered all the questions, click on the Submit Quiz button
to see how you've done, and perhaps get pointers to things you should review.

<div class="quiz-container">

<form id="quizForm">

<div class="question" id="q1">
<h3>1. What is the <em>best</em> way to test the significance of the association between two categorical variables in a two-way frequency table?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q1" value="a" id="q1a"> <label for="q1a">a) Using a chi-square test</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q1" value="b" id="q1b"> <label for="q1b">b) Using a t-test</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q1" value="c" id="q1c"> <label for="q1c">c) Using a one-way ANOVA</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q1" value="d" id="q1d"> <label for="q1d">d) Using a linear regression</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp1"></div>
</div>

<div class="question" id="q2">
<h3>2. What is the best measure used to quantify the <em>strength</em> of association between two categorical variables in a two-way frequency table?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q2" value="a" id="q2a"> <label for="q2a">a) Chi-square test</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q2" value="b" id="q2b"> <label for="q2b">b) Cramer's <em>V</em></label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q2" value="c" id="q2c"> <label for="q2c">c) Pearson's correlation coefficient</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q2" value="d" id="q2d"> <label for="q2d">d) Odds ratio</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q2" value="e" id="q2e"> <label for="q2e">e) None of the above</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp2"></div>
</div>

<div class="question" id="q3">
<h3>3. What is the <em>null hypothesis</em> for a chi-square test of independence in a two-way frequency table?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q3" value="a" id="q3a"> <label for="q3a">a) The two variables are independent</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q3" value="b" id="q3b"> <label for="q3b">b) The two variables are dependent</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q3" value="c" id="q3c"> <label for="q3c">c) The two variables are correlated</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q3" value="d" id="q3d"> <label for="q3d">d) The two variables are not correlated</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp3"></div>
</div>

<div class="question" id="q4">
<h3>4. What is the <em>alternative hypothesis</em> for a chi-square test for independence in a two-way frequency table?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q4" value="a" id="q4a"> <label for="q4a">a) The two variables are independent</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q4" value="b" id="q4b"> <label for="q4b">b) The two variables are dependent</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q4" value="c" id="q4c"> <label for="q4c">c) The two variables are uncorrelated</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q4" value="d" id="q4d"> <label for="q4d">d) None of the above</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp4"></div>
</div>

<div class="question" id="q5">
<h3>5. What are the assumptions for the validity of a chi-square test for independence in a two-way frequency table?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q5" value="a" id="q5a"> <label for="q5a">a) The observations are independent and randomly sampled</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q5" value="b" id="q5b"> <label for="q5b">b) The expected frequencies for each cell in the table are greater than 5</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q5" value="c" id="q5c"> <label for="q5c">c) The variables are categorical</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q5" value="d" id="q5d"> <label for="q5d">d) All of the above</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp5"></div>
</div>

<div class="question" id="q6">
<h3>6. When interpreting the results of a chi-square test for independence in a two-way frequency table, what does a <em>p</em>-value of less than 0.05 indicate?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q6" value="a" id="q6a"> <label for="q6a">a) There is evidence of association between the two variables</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q6" value="b" id="q6b"> <label for="q6b">b) There is no evidence of association between the two variables</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q6" value="c" id="q6c"> <label for="q6c">c) The variables are correlated</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q6" value="d" id="q6d"> <label for="q6d">d) The variables are uncorrelated</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp6"></div>
</div>

<div class="question" id="q7">
<h3>7. How do you interpret the <em>p</em>-value in a chi-squared test for independence in a two-way frequency table?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q7" value="a" id="q7a"> <label for="q7a">a) A small <em>p</em>-value indicates evidence against the null hypothesis</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q7" value="b" id="q7b"> <label for="q7b">b) A large <em>p</em>-value indicates evidence against the null hypothesis</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q7" value="c" id="q7c"> <label for="q7c">c) A small <em>p</em>-value indicates evidence in favor of the null hypothesis</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q7" value="d" id="q7d"> <label for="q7d">d) A large <em>p</em>-value indicates evidence in favor of the null hypothesis</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp7"></div>
</div>

<div class="question" id="q8">
<h3>8. When both variables are <em>ordered</em> in a two-way frequency table, the most focused test for association is:</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q8" value="a" id="q8a"> <label for="q8a">a) The Pearson chi-squared test</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q8" value="b" id="q8b"> <label for="q8b">b) The Likelihood ratio chi-squared test</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q8" value="c" id="q8c"> <label for="q8c">c) The CMH test for general association</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q8" value="d" id="q8d"> <label for="q8d">d) The CMH test for non-zero correlation</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp8"></div>
</div>

</form>

};
